author: Katie Rosendale
title: After fire, family-run restaurant looks to rebuild - NewsBreak
text:
By Katie Rosendale ,
8 hours ago
GRAND RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — Weeks after a “terrifying” fire forced 7 Mares in Grand Rapids to shut down, the family that runs the restaurant is turning to the community for support, with a fundraiser scheduled for this weekend.
7 Mares has been at the corner of Kalamazoo Avenue SE and Adams Street SE since 1999, when Tina Santoyo founded it. More than 27 years later, it remains a family-run community staple, serving authentic Mexican dishes like quesabirrias, tacos, tortas and tilapia.
West Michigan native realizes dream by opening Hudsonville bakery From left to right: Sebastian Santoyo, Tina Santoyo, Lily Arias and Yamilex Santoyo, who run 7 Mares in Grand Rapids. (Aug. 12, 2026) “I grew up here. My parents have owned this restaurant since I was literally not even 5 years old,” said Yamilex Santoyo, who manages, serves at and runs social media for the restaurant. “And it’s a huge part of our community.”
“My mom has worked countless hours, countless days, countless nights, you know, just to have the restaurant up and running,” said sibling Sebastian Santoyo, the restaurant’s chef. “So it means honestly everything to me.”
But around 11:20 a.m. July 21, a fire broke out at the building.
“It was terrifying,” Yamilex Santoyo said. “It was so scary and it was so sad to see our business and our home for so many years in flames.”
Crews douse fire at Mexican restaurant in Grand Rapids Sibling Lily Arias, who now owns the restaurant, told News 8 she was at work at another job when she got the call from her mom.
“I don’t want to get emotional, but it was hard because just seeing all the hard work my mom has put into this business throughout all those years and seeing something like a fire affect us — not only us, but our employees,” Arias said. “It’s heartbreaking.”
Crews arrived on scene within three minutes, found flames coming from the exterior of the second story and began spraying water right away. No one was hurt.
“Thanks to the fire rescue, the fire was put out pretty quickly,” Yamilex Santoyo said. “And it could have been worse.”
“Honestly, I just prayed to God and all my worries went away,” Sebastian Santoyo said. “I’m just glad everybody was OK, everybody made it out safe, nobody got hurt.”
Neighbors concerned as Grand Rapids store seeks approval to sell alcohol at new site Still, the fire — and the water — caused significant damage to 7 Mares, forcing it to close. The damage is largely in the kitchen area, Arias told News 8, but the full extent of the damage isn’t yet clear.
“Unfortunately, it seems like it’s going to be like a long process until we’re able to finally open back up,” she said. “We haven’t got the OK to get the electricity back up, so we haven’t been able to see what equipment is damaged.”
The lack of timeline has been stressful, she continued.
“Everybody in the community is reaching out and wanting to know when we’re going to open up again and come and support,” Arias said. “But the insurance hasn’t provided any estimated time of when we can start repairs yet.”
‘I kept the faith’: Business owner returns to Boston Square with ice cream parlor In the meantime, the family is inviting the community to a fundraiser this weekend. It’s taking place Friday, Saturday and Sunday at Oakdale Park Church at 961 Temple St. SE in Grand Rapids. There, attendees will be able to enjoy a range of dishes, like quesabirrias, tacos and horchata.
“I will be personally cooking all the delicious food for everybody,” Sebastian Santoyo said. “I’m hoping to see all of our great customers that we see all the time, all the community to come and support. And we are super, super, super excited to see everybody.”
Family members will be there to talk with neighbors, and they will also be selling T-shirts with 7 Mares’ logo and the phrase “fueled by our community.” There may also be a “surprise,” the family hinted.
Inside WOODTV.com: Building West Michigan All proceeds will go toward 7 Mares’ rebuilding effort.
“It’s been already three weeks where our employees aren’t receiving any income and we don’t have any income, so it’s to help our employees out and to help us hopefully start rebuilding,” Arias said.
The fundraiser will run from 3 p.m. to 7 p.m. Friday and Saturday and 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday in Oakdale Park Church ’s parking lot.
